others.route: Work permit (temporary permit, Chief Immigration Officer)

note: Niue: the Immigration Act 2011 (Act No. 309) confirms the right of New Zealand citizens born in Niue to travel to and remain there, and of all other New Zealand citizens who aren't prohibited persons, and requires all other persons to hold visas or permits to travel to or remain in Niue (s. 2); every such person must hold a permit to remain lawfully (s. 7), and the work permit is the temporary permit for persons intending to undertake employment or provide any services in Niue (s. 14(7)(a)), applied for on arrival (s. 15). So New Zealand passports are free and every other passport needs the work permit; the Immigration Regulations 2011 exempt listed nationalities only from a visitor's permit of up to 30 days, and set the work permit's fee at NZ$420, which the form doesn't hold. Reading: the Act states New Zealand citizens' right to remain, not to work, in so many words; s. 4(3)'s express freedom to 'undertake any activity' is for those born in Niue. Read in PacLII's copies through archive.org's snapshots (the Act of 20 April 2022, the Regulations of 15 December 2024), since PacLII refuses this client; no later amendment was found in PacLII's Niue list. No days without the permit are named.
